plain_english: Just as omniscience and similar powers arise in a body superintended by this, so through superintendence in one's own self they arise everywhere.
sanskrit_cite: anenādhiṣṭhite dehe yathā sarvajñatādayaḥ tathā svātmany adhiṣṭhānāt sarvatraivam bhaviṣyati

plain_english: Weariness and rolling flow in the body from ignorance of that; if unmeṣa were obliterated, whence would that flow be, causeless?
sanskrit_cite: glānir viluṅthikā dehe tasyāścājñānataḥ sṛtiḥ tad unmeṣaviluptaṃ cet kutaḥ sā syād ahetukā

plain_english: Because for one attached to a single thought there is other-rise, unmeṣa is to be known by oneself; one should recognize him.
sanskrit_cite: ekacintāprasaktasya yataḥ syād aparodayaḥ unmeṣaḥ sa tu vijñeyaḥ svayaṃ tam upalakṣayet

plain_english: Therefore bindu, therefore nāda, form from this, therefore rasa proceed quickly indeed as the agitating of the embodied.
sanskrit_cite: ato bindur ato nādo rūpam asmād ato rasaḥ pravartante 'cireṇaiva kṣobhakatvena dehinaḥ

plain_english: When, with desire to see, one stands pervading all objects, then what need of much said? One will understand by oneself.
sanskrit_cite: didṛkṣayeva sarvārthān yadā vyāpyāvatiṣṭhate tadā kiṃ bahunoktena svayam eva avabhotsyate

plain_english: The awakened should always stand, seeing the range by knowledge and placing all in one; then he is not afflicted by another.
sanskrit_cite: prabuddhaḥ sarvadā tiṣṭhej jñānenālokya gocaram ekatrāropayet sarvaṃ tato 'nyena na pīḍyate

plain_english: He who, with glory obliterated by kalā, has gone into the enjoyability of the power-class arisen from the mass of sound, is called an animal.
sanskrit_cite: śabdarāśisamutthasya śaktivargasya bhogyatām kalāviluptavibhavo gataḥ san sa paśuḥ smṛtaḥ

plain_english: Deprived of supreme nectar-rasa, his cognition-rise leads him by that to non-independence, and he is in the range of tanmātras.
sanskrit_cite: parāmṛtarasāpāyas tasya yaḥ pratyayodbhavaḥ tenāsvatantratām asvatantratām eti sa ca tanmātragocaraḥ

plain_english: In the veiling of his own form, his powers constantly rise, because cognition-rise is not without connection to sound.
sanskrit_cite: svarūpāvaraṇe cāsya asya śaktayaḥ satatotthitāḥ yataḥ śabdānuvedhena na vinā pratyayodbhavaḥ
